reviews.review: yes

I'd recommend anyone who's interested in playing it to wait until it's out of early access when some of the issues has hopefully been ironed out.

Good: 
- The game's story and art is good.
- Decent interface (well coded).

Bad: 
- Puzzles often have unrealistic time limits or forces you to guess the answer, and after the time runs  or you guess wrong you have to rewatch all of the dialogue before the puzzle started.
- Evidence often don't make sense, things that seem irrelevant are often evidence and vice versa.
- Plenty of spelling mistakes.
- The 5th chapter can't be completed at the moment due to a bug,
- The game doesn't reward you for thinking on your own when collecting evidence or hacking people (with a few exceptions).
- There isn't really a difficulty curve and the game never really opens up in terms of gameplay.
reviews.developer_response: Thank you so much for your feedback. My team is working the major bugs, and I will release a new version soon. Once we confirmed the major bugs are fixed, the game will be out of early access.

The game is relatively similar to Orwell, which I enjoyed very much. It got some clever gameplay aspects to it and most of the puzzles are neither too easy nor too hard. The storylines, while a bit predictable at times, are fine and easy enough to follow. Also, the voice actors do a pretty good job for a game of this scope. 

Why the thumbs down then? Because the game really suffers from the fact that the writers and developers don't seem to be fluent in the English language. Unfortunately, this leads to grammatical errors, a strange choice of words and stilted dialogues at every corner, which constantly breaks the immersion and sometimes even makes it hard to understand what the game is trying to tell you. In a game mostly relying on text, this is a huge issue. Getting native speakers on board to help with the translation could help a great deal, I think. Considering this game is in Early Access, I'd gladly turn this negative review into a positive one, if the language problem gets fixed.
reviews.developer_response: Thank you so much for your feedback. I am so sorry about the translation problem. I have to say English is not our native language, but my team will try our best to fix the issue. Also there are some guys are willing to help us.

Overall a good game, especially if you enjoyed Orwell and Hypnospace Outlaw. Here the major focus is on compiling peoples information, so that you can generate their passwords and find out more about them. All that works well enough and it's fun working out what happened, along with how everyone connects together.

However the game does have some issues that stuck out to me:
The first chapters has a poorer English translation, than the rest. It's not so bad that you can't understand whats going on, but it's still kind of annoying.
While the translation improves, a few issues do creep in later on, such as a female character being referred to as 'he' in a phone call, or the voiced dialogue not quite matching the text.
Considering the type of game, it was probably inevitable but I sometime found myself pouring over everything trying to find the one piece of information I needed to continue.
Sometimes, even when I had collected enough data, the related event would fail to trigger, leaving me unable to progress. I was always able to reload an auto-save, and the event would then play normally, but it often took me a few minutes to realise I needed to do this.
One type of puzzle , is a mobile phone lock-screen which was very annoying to solve. Even with a clue it was tedious to work out the answer, resulting in a lot of guess-work. It also was done under a time-limit.

It's still a good game despite these issues, and I look forward to more content being added in future.

Better translation and voice direction would go a long way to improving future versions.

I am a big fan of adventure games since the early 90s.Any game that uses your mind to work things out be it in graphical and text or animated. The game is great to put on in the evening when all is quite, have your glass of malibu and coke and try crack the cases. The game is a mixture of detective cyber hunt using all the tools available to track, trace and gather evidence to complete the chapters. WIth the use of social media in all our lives this is  glimpse of what can be found online and how scary things can be online but its a great version in a game. Once of the only things i can say is if you have seen the film searching and you liked it then you have to play this game ( cant help thinking about the similarities in the way you search for stuff and also the title music very similar, but this is a good thing as i loved the film ( a must see ) and this game puts me in that mode and a great buy. I can see this going further and further with the introduction of more cases never ending. The play time is very good and cases are quite diverse and expanding. THere is a great urgency to complete the cases and with each development there is a twist . Detective cyber hacker all in one. Its presented in a lovely way with with great touched to the social media sites online with a great internet browse search engine along with other tools to play the game. Looking through transcripts and reports with what ever you find to gather the clues and come to a conclusion really keeps you on your toes. You can not go wrong for the price and if your worried play the demo like i did once you get to as far as you can with the demo you will want more and end up purchasing the full game. ( as developer says remember the saved game in the demo will not work with the full game) So if you get the idea of the game quite early on buy it and start a new game. I played to the end of the demo and loved it so much and wanted more that i sacrificed to play all the up to that point again and completed the first chapter. My play time on the chapter was 58 out of 58 information gathered with a play time of around an hour  each evening spanning over a few days with some extra play time in between as i wanted to see what happens next. Play the demo like what you see in the first 15 mins then go straight to the purchase

So, I got this game because it reminded me a lot of Orwell. I've grown to like playing detective games where you learn more about others through their media and all that. And yeah, I know this is a hacking game and different, but it's clear this game was inspired by Orwell, at least to me it was. Now, first going into this, the game was kind of fun. Simple, but fun. It does seem to get harder as you go along and it's interesting to learn more about the chapter your in. 

However, the game has two major problems for me. First off, the interface is a bit annoying. Like, to erase something, you need to actually hit your own delete button. I know this may be nitpicking, but you don't have to do this when copying and pasting, and you are going to be doing a lot of these two. It's also tedious going through the apps. When closing them, for example, you have to recopy  the password in should you need to go back to the same users file. 

Another thing that makes this game a bit annoying for me is the tutorial. This game, unless your good with tech and/or hacking, doesn't do a good job at explaining certain aspects of the game. A good example of this is when you need to hack into someone's phone in chapter two. It's also vaguely explains certain things later in the game and this is done by your jerk of the boss. I don't get this since the beginning had a pretty nice tutorial. 

I don't want to say it's a bad game. It's not actually. But honestly, the interface and lacking tutorial for later and important parts of the game make this not fun for me. If you're someone who doesn't care much for these things or good with tech/hacking,  I'll think you'll enjoy it. The game is lacking a bit though in terms of really getting into these peoples' life and getting to know them. I wish it had done more of that because the chapters are interesting. Still, I'll change my review should these two things be changed (or at least the interface.) It's not a bad game and is decent, but for me at the moment I don't want to keep playing it.

Honestly for an EA game, this has potential.
-Well acted voice overs where appropriate
-Excellent little mini-games and timed sections which break up the regular pacing of the game for a small hint of excitement
-Comfortable UI and UX aspects.

However, that does not mean that the game is free of bugs, nor does not need some shine and polishing in other areas.
-The localisation for English needs a lot of work. I understand and appreciate that English may not be the primary language of the devs, it can be jarring and de-imsersifying (probably just created a word there) in places where the flow and writing gets jumbled, lacks conveyance and flow. -If- English is going to be the primary release language, then additional work needs to be done polishing that up, as reading through news stories, toothbook posts and hitalk app conversations are so critical to gameplay in Cyber Manhunter. 

- While the gameplay is interesting, and slowly reveals itself over time, save for a few set pieces (phone trojans, the chapter 3 end setpiece, and phone conversations) the gameplay is very samey: 
      - Get information on Person A
      - Crack Person A's stuff using the database to get incomplete information Person B 
      - Rinse and repeat for B to C and so on. 
Don't get me wrong this is a fine mechanic core mechanic but in the second and third chapters (which are where the breaks from core mechanics really should be kicking in) there's not enough divergence from that key mechanic which in my opinion mutes the game just a little bit. 

- Finally: Replayability at this point is low. 4 hours in and with enough snooping and combing through what is a series of engrossing stories, I can truthfully say there's nothing to come back to for now. Certainly if you just focused on drilling down exactly what you needed for the main objective of each chapter you would find that yeah, coming back to perfect a chapter would be worthwhile, but then after that you're pretty much done. 
I'm not sure if its on the horizon or not, but something that could randomise a mission, or a free play or something that would beef-up the very nicely put together experience that is Cyber Manhunter and keep me playing it longer would be appreciated, as I thoroughly enjoyed my Friday night with it. 

I know it looks like I've gone into more detail with the current drawbacks than I have the pros of the game, however what Cyber Manhunter does right it does beautifully. This review is more....feedback than anything else, and hopefully something the devs see. For you the player, this is definitely something you can pick up, play and get hooked into. A good Friday night relaxing beer and investigate game that makes you think. Well worth the price of admission at this point and I look forward to what is provided by the developers moving forward.

Even though it's not perfect I really recommend the game, also cause it's for a small coin. But instead of giving a full review I just write what issues the game has as it is still work in progress:

I really loved the investigation parts like looking up stuff but I felt that there was not all possibilities used. Like in the last episode where Cyclops wasn't mentioned as a character even though he was one of the prime persons. I would have loved to get into his case as side investigation instead of having him just as a pressure against Isabelle. The last investigation felt off overall, where I saw the lack of information on major stuff. Like they talk about the lost person but not the fire, you also couldn't "gogo" the fire. The situation was pretty complex where I saw that the information also has to get more complex as well but it stayed the same amount as the other cases. So I would look at the cases and think about what the players might look for and provide some information even though it gets nowhere like the novel with its summary. That was a good example, interesting to read and giving the idea what may have happened. 

Secondly I didn't like the phone calls, they felt like try and error for the most time and in many cases it didn't make sense that the other side just cut the line and you get yelled by your boss. Dialogue systems like these need more finesse, you still can bring other arguments until you completely mess it up. One good thing was the girl which you had to bring into almost a mental breakdown to get your information. But instead of being just hit or miss you need maybe to say: 70% of the choices are enough for your goal, so you can like mess up 1 or 2 choices and still win. That feels more RPG like in these situations, you just don't get burned to dust instantly if your counterpart gets an answer he/she doesn't like. 

Thirdly the hacks of the phones have been a bit strange. I don't even know why you don't have much time, cause it makes no sense. Its not like the user of the phone is counter hacking or whatever. But yeah I understand the urge to make it difficult through that. Just a bit waste of the nice informations inside the phone. The idea of finding swipes was cool but the one of Jim made me crazy that the "2" was a part of starting at the second dot of the swiping patern was a critical one. The rainbow one was far more intuitive. The main issue in puzzle games is when the puzzles start to make not much sense in a logical chain. And this one was pretty close to that imo still I got it after some time, but phew. Then the time issue is really annoying going through the whole "hacking in" again. Instead of the time trial I would rather fill the phone with more information where you have to dig through to get what I want. Don't know if it's too much to ask for but that would be just my idea of making that part more enjoyable than stressful and annoying sometimes.

As I said the game overall is super interesting, like Welcome to the Game without murderers, just investigation how many fans of WttG wished for. I hope it goes on. I played the cases again to get missing info etc. Just my type of game. Keep up the good work.
